A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Steerable Transformers for Volumetric Data. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C support comparison, including matching content across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification and segmentation experiments on Rotated MNIST, ModelNet10, PH2 and BraTS in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experimental results and additionally reports average training and inference runtimes per batch in Table 1.

M1.justification: The steerable convolution–transformer architecture, positional encoding, attention equations, Fourier nonlinearities and normalization procedure remain unchanged. The new positional-encoding illustration does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four datasets and tasks, including ModelNet10 with z-axis and SO(3) rotations. Revised segmentation illustrations and added runtime measurements do not establish new dataset or test-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Steerable convolutions remain the comparator in Tables 1–2. Tables 3–4 retain the same external comparison methods, including GSA-Nets and GE-ViT for Rotated MNIST, and ECC, SO-Net and Cubenet for ModelNet10.

E3.justification: Table 1 adds average training and inference runtime per batch as evaluation measures. Existing data splits, rotation procedures, training schedules, batch sizes, model configurations and accuracy/Dice metrics remain unchanged. A detailed timing procedure is not supplied.

E4.justification: The qualitative segmentation evidence is revised: v2 Figures 3 and 5 become v3 Figures 4 and 6 with different displayed BraTS views, masks and probability maps. This changes the illustrated prediction examples without establishing new experiments. The radial-resolution/Fourier-cutoff sweeps and attention-head analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain mean and standard deviation reporting over five runs. No changed seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are documented. The added runtime columns provide averages without a separately specified uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: Accuracy, Dice, parameter counts and comparative scores in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. Table 1 adds runtime results: for BraTS, convolution and transformer training/inference batch times are respectively 5.04/1.00 s and 5.37/1.01 s. Segmentation panels also change, without establishing a same-setting predictive-performance gain.

T1.justification: Equation (1) removes the extraneous outer integral over SO(d). Section 3.5 changes the condition for simplifying complexity to O(NC²) from N much smaller than C to N and C of comparable order. The equivariance proposition and Appendix B proof are retained, with renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: SE(d)-equivariant attention over steerable convolutional features and improved classification/segmentation through the hybrid architecture. The shortened abstract opening does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.5 revises the applicability regime of its convolution-cost comparison from sequences much shorter than the channel dimension to comparable sizes. Predictive-result interpretations and the explicit memory and Fourier-cutoff limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 adds an explicit code-repository link. Appendix C retains the existing dataset-access links, optimizer schedules, batch sizes, total training times and 16GB GPU descriptions. The PDFs establish the new access pointer, not the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to earlier equivariant attention and convolution methods remain unchanged. Numerous bibliography URLs are omitted in v3, but their corresponding references are retained.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the abstract opening, revises front matter and heading conventions, and adds a code-access sentence and a brief Impact Statement. Most prose and the order of the scientific sections and appendices remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adopts conference formatting with substantially rearranged front matter and figure placement. It adds the positional-encoding diagram, revises both segmentation figures, and expands Table 1 with training/inference columns. The architecture, attention-map and ModelNet10 illustrations are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 provides useful additional transparency through per-batch runtime comparisons and a code-access link, while the positional-encoding diagram and corrected Equation (1) improve exposition and mathematical precision. Benchmark scores, ablations and the main scaling limitations remain unchanged, and revised segmentation panels do not establish better performance. These are evidence-supported but limited overall gains.
